scenes.tts: The tube closes very early. So when does prevention have to start?
scenes.visual: Title card: Four Weeks, and a Vitamin. A timeline with a closed tube at its end.
scenes.narration: The tube closes very early. So when does prevention have to start?

scenes.tts: Embryologists date human embryos by Carnegie stages, defined by structure, not by age.
scenes.visual: A row of embryo outlines labelled Carnegie stages. On screen: folds first meet, about stage 10; head-end neuropore closes, about 11; tail-end neuropore closes, about 12 to 13.
scenes.narration: Embryologists date human embryos by Carnegie stages, defined by structure, not by age.

scenes.tts: Counted from fertilization, primary closure is complete by the end of about the fourth week.
scenes.visual: Upper clock: days after fertilization. A marker at about day 28: primary closure complete.
scenes.narration: Counted from fertilization, primary closure is complete by the end of about the fourth week.

scenes.tts: Doctors count pregnancy from the last menstrual period. That clock starts about two weeks earlier.
scenes.visual: Lower clock: weeks of pregnancy, starting about two weeks before fertilization.
scenes.narration: Doctors count pregnancy from the last menstrual period. That clock starts about two weeks earlier.

scenes.tts: Predict. On the doctor's clock, how far along is the pregnancy when the tube has closed?
scenes.visual: Pause card: Predict. Weeks of pregnancy at closure? The lower clock's marker is blank.
scenes.narration: Predict. On the doctor's clock, how far along is the pregnancy when the tube has closed?

scenes.tts: About six weeks of pregnancy. Many pregnancies are not yet recognized at that point.
scenes.visual: The lower clock marker fills: about 6 weeks. A band labelled: many pregnancies not yet recognized.
scenes.narration: About six weeks of pregnancy. Many pregnancies are not yet recognized at that point.

scenes.tts: So the vitamin has to be there already.
scenes.visual: Caption: prevention has to be in place before closure.
scenes.narration: So the vitamin has to be there already.

scenes.tts: The first trial enrolled women who had already had an affected pregnancy, so their risk was high.
scenes.visual: Credit: Medical Research Council Vitamin Study, 1991. Women with a previous affected pregnancy; folic acid, 4 milligrams a day, from before conception.
scenes.narration: The first trial enrolled women who had already had an affected pregnancy, so their risk was high.

scenes.tts: Folic acid, started before conception, cut recurrence by about seventy-two percent.
scenes.caption: Folic acid, started before conception, cut recurrence by about 72 percent.
scenes.visual: On screen: about 72 percent fewer recurrences.
scenes.narration: Folic acid, started before conception, cut recurrence by about 72 percent.

scenes.tts: Were seventy-two of every hundred women spared? No. That is a relative change.
scenes.caption: Were 72 of every 100 women spared? No. That is a relative change.
scenes.visual: Two labels: relative change, absolute change. Relative is highlighted.
scenes.narration: Were 72 of every 100 women spared? No. That is a relative change.

scenes.tts: Without folic acid, about three and a half in a hundred pregnancies were affected. With it, about one.
scenes.caption: Without folic acid, about 3.5 in 100 pregnancies were affected. With it, about 1.
scenes.visual: Two bars: about 3.5 in 100 without folic acid, about 1 in 100 with it.
scenes.narration: Without folic acid, about 3.5 in 100 pregnancies were affected. With it, about 1.

scenes.tts: The absolute fall was about two and a half percentage points. The relative figure alone does not say how many women benefit.
scenes.caption: The absolute fall was about 2.5 percentage points. The relative figure alone does not say how many women benefit.
scenes.visual: The gap between the bars is labelled: about 2.5 percentage points fewer. Beside it: about 72 percent fewer, relative.
scenes.narration: The absolute fall was about 2.5 percentage points. The relative figure alone does not say how many women benefit.

scenes.tts: But most affected babies have mothers with no earlier affected pregnancy. Can a first case be prevented?
scenes.visual: A large group of women with no previous affected pregnancy; a question mark.
scenes.narration: But most affected babies have mothers with no earlier affected pregnancy. Can a first case be prevented?

scenes.tts: In Hungary, women planning a pregnancy took a multivitamin with folic acid, or trace elements.
scenes.visual: Credit: Czeizel and Dudás, 1992. Two groups: multivitamin with 0.8 milligrams of folic acid; trace elements.
scenes.narration: In Hungary, women planning a pregnancy took a multivitamin with folic acid, or trace elements.

scenes.tts: There were six affected pregnancies in the trace-element group, and none with the multivitamin.
scenes.visual: On screen: trace elements, 6 affected; multivitamin, 0.
scenes.narration: There were six affected pregnancies in the trace-element group, and none with the multivitamin.

scenes.tts: But the numbers were small, and a multivitamin cannot credit folic acid alone.
scenes.visual: Two caveat tags: small numbers; a multivitamin, not folic acid alone.
scenes.narration: But the numbers were small, and a multivitamin cannot credit folic acid alone.

scenes.tts: Folic acid lowers the risk; it does not remove it. Most mothers of affected babies are not folate deficient by ordinary tests.
scenes.visual: Open-question card: Folic acid lowers risk, does not remove it.
scenes.narration: Folic acid lowers the risk; it does not remove it. Most mothers of affected babies are not folate deficient by ordinary tests.

scenes.tts: In mice, some mutants respond to folate and others do not. How folate prevents defects is still not known.
scenes.visual: Two mouse icons: folate-responsive, folate-resistant. Card: How does folate work? Not known.
scenes.narration: In mice, some mutants respond to folate and others do not. How folate prevents defects is still not known.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: the tube often closes before a woman knows she is pregnant. So folic acid must come first.
scenes.visual: Closing card: closure by about week 6 of pregnancy; folic acid before conception.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: the tube often closes before a woman knows she is pregnant. So folic acid must come first.
